title: Essential: Final Ratio
description: Essential Criteria: The final answer must be the correct numerical ratio I1/I2 = √2 / 2.

title: Important: Force in Case 1
description: Important Criteria: Correctly identifies the Coulomb force as the centripetal force for the single-charge case (F1 = kQe/r²).

title: Important: Force in Case 2
description: Important Criteria: Correctly calculates the net Coulomb force on the electron from two charges, including vector addition and the 30° angle (F2 = √3 kQe/r²).

title: Important: Radius in Case 2
description: Important Criteria: Correctly determines the radius of the circular orbit in the two-charge case using geometry (r' = r cos 30° = √3 r / 2).

title: Important: Relating Period to Current
description: Important Criteria: Applies the definition of equivalent current (I = e/T) for both cases and relates it to centripetal force via T.

title: Optional: Algebraic Derivation
description: Optional Criteria: Shows clear algebraic combination of force, centripetal acceleration, and current definitions to derive expressions for I1 and I2.

title: Pitfall: Force Direction/Sign
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly treats the force as repulsive or misapplies the sign of the electron's charge in the force calculation.

title: Pitfall: Geometry Error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student uses an incorrect angle (e.g., 60°) or wrong radius (e.g., r' = r) for the two-charge case.
